public_rationale: In its usual sense, tokenmaxxing means the 2026 workplace push to maximize AI token use. A New York Times report from June 2026 says the tokenmaxxing era 'appears to be over'. Meta said it would limit AI use, Uber and Walmart capped AI spending, and Amazon and Meta took down their token-use leaderboards. A later LeadDev report agrees the trend collapsed quickly. So the core claim holds for the weeks around the post. Two caveats. Total spending on tokens kept growing: Anthropic's annualized revenue rate passed $65 billion by July. And some firms still tracked token use. So what died was the practice and its leaderboards, not token consumption. The aside that Marcus and Eisman predicted this was not scored.
limitations: Relies on news reports, not company documents.
The NYT report came out 11 days after the post, but it describes June conditions.
'Died' has no measure; some organizations still track token use.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Tokenmaxxing has clearly died, as Marcus and Eisman anticipated.

statement.excerpt: First of all, domino one: tokenmaxxing has indeed clearly died, just as Eisman and I had anticipated a few weeks ago.
statement.document_title: Breaking news, and how the end might begin

from_speaker: just as Eisman and I had anticipated a few weeks ago
our_interpretation: Tokenmaxxing is read in its common sense: the 2026 practice, pushed by employers and leaderboards, of maximizing AI token use as a sign of productivity.
'Clearly died' is read as: by around the post date, major adopters had publicly reversed the practice (leaderboards removed, spending capped) and informed observers described the trend as over.
Target period is May to June 2026, the weeks around the post. Reports published shortly after the post that describe the state in June are counted.
The aside that Marcus and Eisman 'anticipated' this is not scored. It concerns the speaker's own earlier statements, which cannot be cited as evidence.
criteria.support_condition: Credible reports from May–June 2026 that major companies dropped token-use leaderboards or capped AI spending, and that observers described the tokenmaxxing trend as over.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible reports from May–June 2026 that employers were still widely encouraging maximal token use, with no notable reversal.

evidence.publisher: The Star (syndicating The New York Times)
evidence.explanation: Concrete reversals at Meta, Uber, Walmart and Amazon in May–June 2026: spending caps and leaderboards taken down.

evidence.excerpt: Indeed, the tokenmaxxing bubble appeared to burst almost as quickly as it emerged.
evidence.locator: section 'The tokenmaxxing bubble has burst', paragraph 2
